summary.text: A dwarf galaxy is a small galaxy of about 1,000 up to several billion stars, compared with the Milky Way's 100 to 400 billion.
Their formation and activity are thought to be heavily influenced by interactions with larger galaxies, and some have been seen pulled apart by neighbouring spirals.
Many dwarf galaxies in the Local Group orbit larger galaxies, and more than 20 known dwarfs orbit the Milky Way.

items.prompt: Two big galaxies collide, and their gravity tugs streams of material away from both. What can come of that debris?

options.label: A larger elliptical galaxy
A tidal dwarf galaxy
Nothing new, since the streams fall back
Only a cloud of dark matter

items.explain: Tidal dwarf galaxies are produced when galaxies collide and their gravitational masses interact, pulling streams of material away.

items.prompt: Two faint, compact groupings of stars look alike. One is a globular cluster and the other an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy. What separates them?

options.label: The dwarf galaxy holds much dark matter and is more extended
The cluster holds much dark matter and is more extended
The dwarf galaxy is much younger and brighter
They differ in nothing but their names

items.explain: Ultra-faint dwarfs resemble globular clusters but contain a significant amount of dark matter and are more extended.

items.prompt: A small galaxy glows blue. What does that tell you about its stars?

options.label: They are mostly old, cool stars
They are spread thinly with no clusters
It contains clusters of young, hot, massive stars
It contains very few stars

items.explain: Blue compact dwarfs hold large clusters of young, hot, massive stars, the brightest of which are blue.

items.prompt: The largest globular cluster in the Milky Way may not be a cluster at all. What do astronomers now think it is?

options.label: A huge region of gas and dust
The core of an absorbed dwarf galaxy with a black hole
A group of stars born in the last billion years
A cluster formed by two spiral galaxies merging

items.explain: Omega Centauri is thought to be the core of a dwarf galaxy with a black hole, absorbed by the Milky Way.

items.prompt: A dwarf galaxy is described as quenched. What would you see in it?

options.label: Very little star formation
Furious star formation
A growing halo of new satellites
Streams of stars being pulled away

items.explain: Quenched dwarf galaxies are ones with little star formation.

items.prompt: Why do astronomers measure the motions of individual stars in nearby dwarf galaxies such as the Sculptor Dwarf?

options.label: To count how many stars the Milky Way holds
To test predictions of the standard cosmological model
To find the age of the Sun
To locate the Galactic Center

items.explain: Those measurements have allowed scientists to test predictions of the standard cosmological model.
